Hi everyone,

I'm currently working on the formalization of group theory related to CFSG. While checking the existing library, I noticed that CompositionSeries.jordan_holder is already implemented, and the instance JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) appears in a TODO list. However, after reviewing the current repository and open PRs, I haven't found implementations for:

  • a classical composition series API for general groups;
  • an interpretation of the abstract JordanHolderLattice.Iso as concrete quotient group isomorphisms.

To fill this gap, I have formalized the following:

  • some foundational concepts, including maximal normal inclusions and the associated quotient groups for subgroup intervals;

  • two types of series:

    1. classical composition series, where each $H_i$ is maximal normal in $H_{i+1}$, together with the Jordan–Hölder theorem (series with the same endpoints have equal length, and the corresponding quotient factors $H_{i+1} / H_i$ are isomorphic up to permutation);
    2. chief series, where each $H_i$ is normal in the ambient group $G$, together with the corresponding Jordan–Hölder uniqueness result (again, equal length and isomorphism of quotient factors up to permutation).

Before proceeding, I have a few questions about mathlib conventions:

  1. Should NormalSubgroup be introduced as a new bundled structure, or is the current predicate-based approach preferred?
  2. Is it desirable to register JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) as a global instance?
  3. What would be the recommended naming and file placement for Subgroup.IsMaximalNormal?

Additionally, is anyone else already working on this? Would it be appropriate to start with a small PR containing Subgroup.IsMaximalNormal and the JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) instance?

Any comments or suggestions would be greatly appreciated—thanks in advance!

Cool!

  1. IMO a bundled version alongside the unbundled version would be nice if it forms a CompleteLattice (similar to TopologicalSpace.IsOpen + TopologicalSpace.Opens, and many others), and also one for characteristic subgroups
  2. No, it would conflict with the existing instance when the group is commutative, but maybe the bundled version could have one
  3. How are you defining IsMaximalNormal? Is it fun N H ↦ Maximal (fun K ↦ K.Normal ∧ K ≤ H) N? Or maybe with < instead? Or with subgroupOf? What are the pros/cons of each choice and what are you planning to do with this predicate? (with the bundled version I believe you could just use CovBy for the JordanHolderLattice instance)
if we register Subgroup G as a JordanHolderLattice do we get a diamond in the case of abelian G since in that case Subgroup G is a IsModularLattice?
(see point 2)

Diwen Yu said:

Additionally, is anyone else already working on this?

Coincidentally, I've noticed this a week ago and wanted to fix it, but since then I got derailed to thinking about the more general IsModularLattice/DistribLattice and am now deep in a rabbit hole of exploring lattice properties :)
does that mean the instance giving JordanHolderLattice from IsModularLattice is a bad instance? cc @Thomas Browning

Oof, yeah, didn't realize that there would be a diamond here. Maybe neither should be an instance then, since there isn't a canonical choice for the IsMaximal predicate in the case of subgroups of an abelian group? (or rather, the two options are propeq but not defeq).

I think CovBy is a very natural choice and the instance is nice (I believe Submodules use it?).
If we define a bundled type for normal subgroup, won't CovBy be exactly the predicate we want?

Thanks for the suggestion, @Snir Broshi ! I have made some changes.

My current approach is as follows:

  • I implemented a bundled NormalSubgroup G, including coercions and a CompleteLattice instance. I also proved IsModularLattice (NormalSubgroup G), so the general modular-lattice instance supplies JordanHolderLattice (NormalSubgroup G), with IsMaximal definitionally equal to CovBy. I use this for the chief-series API.

  • I do not register a classical JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) instance, since that would create a typeclass diamond. Moreover, NormalSubgroup G describes chief series, whose terms are all normal in the fixed ambient group, but not classical composition series, where each term need only be normal in the next one.

For classical composition series, I currently use:

def IsMaximalNormal (H K : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  H < K ∧ ∃ hN : (H.subgroupOf K).Normal,
    letI := hN
    IsSimpleGroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K)

I proved equivalent characterizations via the absence of a proper intermediate subgroup normal in K, and via CovBy from the bundled H.subgroupOf K to ⊤ in NormalSubgroup K. The API currently includes iff_quotient_isSimple, iff_eq_or_eq, iff_not_exists, and iff_covBy.

I chose the quotient-based definition because it keeps the normality witness readily available, whereas a CovBy-based definition would require repeatedly bundling H.subgroupOf K. However, CovBy fits the generic Jordan–Hölder API more directly.

I would appreciate opinions on three design choices:

  1. Should IsMaximalNormal be defined using the simple quotient, an intermediate-subgroup maximality condition, or directly using CovBy in NormalSubgroup K?
  2. For classical composition series, should the required JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) be a named non-instance value, a scoped/local instance, or constructed only where needed?
  3. For an initial PR, should I submit only NormalSubgroup and its complete-lattice API, or include the modular-lattice instance as well?
Not fully answering these questions, but the strict inequality H < K is already implied by IsSimpleGroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K).
Indeed, thanks! I will replace H < K by H ≤ K.

I think JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) should be an instance, and the current IsMaximalNormal is a good definition to serve as its IsMaximal relation. This is the most general definition when it comes to subgroups (with operators) in a group. NormalSubgroupand Submodule are both examples of subgroups with operators, where the operators (can be formalized as (Mul)DistribMulAction by a Monoid, or just DistribSMul) is the ambient group acting by conjugation in the former case and the ring action in the latter case. Whenever the operators contain all conjugations, the lattice becomes modular, and normality in the IsMaximal relation becomes automatic. (For Submodule the conjugations are all trivial as the ambient additive group is abelian.) For these lattices it's reasonable to use the constructor of JordanHolderLattice from IsModularLattice (and obtain CovBy as the IsMaximal relation), but this constructor shouldn't be an instance (to avoid the diamond). For Subgroup of an abelian group, we can just add a lemma stating IsMaximal is equivalent to CovBy.

One can still prove a Jordan-Holder theorem when the operators don't contain all conjugations but aren't all trivial, though I don't know if such examples have ever been studied.

Thanks, this seems compatible with most of my current API: the existing IsMaximalNormal can serve as the classical IsMaximal relation on Subgroup G, while NormalSubgroup G can continue to use CovBy.

If I understand correctly, the proposed instance design is:

  • JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G) is the global instance, with IsMaximal := IsMaximalNormal;
  • the construction from IsModularLattice remains available as a named constructor, but is no longer a global instance;
  • concrete modular lattices such as NormalSubgroup G and Submodule R M register their own JordanHolderLattice instances using that constructor;
  • for an abelian group, one proves that IsMaximalNormal is equivalent to CovBy, rather than obtaining a second instance.

This differs from the current upstream state after #41445, where

[IsModularLattice X] → JordanHolderLattice X

is registered globally as an instance. With that instance present, registering the classical structure on Subgroup G would create the diamond discussed above, so my current named non-instance structure is a workaround for the existing upstream design.

Are you suggesting that the modular-lattice construction should be changed upstream from an instance into a named constructor? If so, I agree that this would give a cleaner global instance for Subgroup G.
First PR #42299, including NormalSubgroup and its complete lattice and modular lattice structures.

For posterity, I have an open PR (#41424) which defines a modular lattice structure on Subobject A for any object A in an abelian category, with a JordanHolderLattice instance then inherited from CovBy

I asked about exactly this one month ago :) #Is there code for X? > JordanHolder in abelian category
Aristotle's solution is ~150 lines but you probably have more complete API
I think I started working on this just a few days before you posted that!
